memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob set up a stone pillar at the place where God had talked with him, and he poured out a drink offering on it; he also poured oil on it. Jacob called the place where God had talked with him Bethel." - Gen 35:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In response to God's appearing, Jacob sets up a stone pillar and pours out offerings upon it — a drink offering of wine and a pouring of oil. Years before, at this same Bethel, Jacob had set up a pillar and poured oil on it (Gen 28:18). Now he does it again, but with even more. His worship has grown richer over the years. He is not just marking a place; he is pouring out something costly before God.

There is something beautiful about a poured-out offering. Unlike a gift you set down and can take back, a drink offering poured on a stone is gone — it cannot be recovered. It is a picture of holding nothing back, of giving to God in a way that leaves no room for second thoughts.

This is the kind of worship God delights in — not merely words, but a life poured out before Him. The apostle Paul described his own life this way, as "being poured out like a drink offering" in service to God (Phil 2:17). And it flows from the greater truth that Christ poured out His life for us.

How do we worship God? Do we offer Him only convenient scraps, or do we pour ourselves out — our time, our love, our very lives? Jacob returned to Bethel and gave God more than before. May our worship, too, grow richer over the years, until our whole life becomes an offering poured out for Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is my worship a poured-out offering, or just convenient scraps?
2. Has my devotion to God grown richer over the years?
3. What would it mean to pour my whole life out before Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, receive my worship as an offering poured out before You. Let my devotion grow richer over the years, until my whole life is given to You, in response to Christ who poured Himself out for me. Amen.
